name: Knave of Hearts
sample_note: Two spoken lines only (ch012-d0033, ch012-d0049). In ch008 he answers the Queen with a bow and a smile (ch008-p13) and obeys an order without a word (ch008-p21-p22). Rules going beyond those lines are tagged inferred:true.

register.level: the court servant's formal deference, turned into a careful defendant's plea
register.summary: A man who survives by saying as little as possible. In the procession he only bows and smiles; on trial he speaks twice, both times short and on the defensive: an exact court formula (Please your Majesty) followed by a denial built like a lawyer's point (I didn't write it, and they can't prove I did: there's no name signed), and a sad rhetorical question that sidesteps the King (Do I look like it?). Per SUP-002/SUP-004 a human performer in flat card-suited page livery; in chains in ch011-ch012.

examples.text: Please your Majesty, I didn't write it, and they can't prove I did: there's no name signed at the end.

catchphrases.text: they can't prove … (denial on the evidence)

sentence_style.length: short: 5 and 20 words; new lines should stay under 20 words and never become a speech

patterns.rule: Opens any address to royalty with the court formula 'Please your Majesty' — deference first, content second.
Defends on the evidence, never on innocence: denies the specific act and points to what cannot be proved (no name signed).

examples.text: I didn't write it, and they can't prove I did: there's no name signed at the end.

patterns.rule: Deflects dangerous questions with a mild rhetorical question about himself instead of a yes/no answer; said 'sadly' (ch012-p51).
Before the trial he answers royalty wordlessly (a bow, a smile, a careful obedient action). If a screenplay line is needed there, it is a two-to-four-word acknowledgement such as 'Yes, your Majesty.'
patterns.reason: ch008 gives him no words (ch008-p13 bows and smiles; ch008-p22 turns the gardeners over 'very carefully, with one foot'); the rule keeps any added line consistent with his trial formula.

examples.text: (narrative) She said it to the Knave of Hearts, who only bowed and smiled in reply.
(narrative) The Knave did so, very carefully, with one foot.

preferred_fields: evidence and proof (the letter, handwriting, signature)

examples.text: there's no name signed at the end.

address.to_the_king_and_queen: your Majesty (always in the formula 'Please your Majesty')
address.to_accusers: they (never names or addresses them directly)

examples.text: Please your Majesty, … they can't prove I did

forbidden_words.reason: the source never has him admit the theft; the trial collapses unresolved (ch012) — a confession would change the plot
he survives by deference; defiance at the trial belongs to Alice (ch012-p62)

drift.change: Procession and croquet-ground: silent servant — bows, smiles, obeys.
In chains at the trial: finds a voice only to defend himself, carefully and briefly, and 'sadly' once the King turns on him.
